title: Qatar Joins Coalition Against Iraqi Invasion of Kuwait
reason: Qatar was one of 39 coalition members opposing Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990, opening its territory to foreign troops on 27 August 1990 and contributing forces to Joint Forces East Command.

title: Qatari Forces Fight at Battle of Khafji
reason: Two Qatari tank companies equipped with AMX-30 tanks fought alongside Saudi National Guard to retake Khafji from Iraqi forces in late January–early February 1991; Saudi and Qatari forces suffered 18 killed and 50 wounded.

title: Qatar-Bahrain Territorial Dispute Escalates to ICJ
reason: Qatar filed an application at the International Court of Justice on 8 July 1991 instituting proceedings against Bahrain over sovereignty of the Hawar Islands, Dibal shoals, and maritime delimitation.

title: Border Clash with Saudi Arabia at Al-Khafous
reason: Qatari and Saudi troops clashed at the Al-Khufus border post in late September 1992, resulting in deaths; the Washington Post reported the incident on 1 October 1992 with Qatar accusing Saudi Arabia of attacking its post.

title: Hamad bin Khalifa Seizes Power in Bloodless Coup
reason: Crown Prince Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani deposed his father Emir Khalifa in a bloodless coup on 27 June 1995 while the emir was vacationing in Geneva; widely reported and confirmed by Wikipedia's dedicated article.

title: Counter-Coup Attempt Foiled
reason: A failed counter-coup attempt to restore Emir Khalifa was foiled on 14 February 1996; 33 plotters were eventually sentenced to life imprisonment in 2000, and investigations implicated connections to regional powers.

title: Al Jazeera Satellite News Network Launches
reason: Al Jazeera Arabic launched on 1 November 1996 as the first independent Arabic-language satellite news channel, funded by a Qatari government grant of approximately $137 million.

title: First LNG Export Shipment to Japan
reason: Qatar's first LNG carrier departed Ras Laffan in December 1996 delivering a cargo to Chubu Electric Power's Kawagoe Terminal in Japan under a 25-year, 4 million tonne/year supply agreement.

title: Education City Project Inaugurated by Qatar Foundation
reason: Qatar Foundation launched Education City in 1997, with Virginia Commonwealth University opening its campus that year as the first institution; the project was spearheaded by Sheikha Moza bint Nasser.

title: Qatar Grants Women Voting Rights in Municipal Elections
reason: Qatar held its first Central Municipal Council elections on 8 March 1999 (International Women's Day) granting women equal right to vote and stand as candidates, making it the first GCC state to do so.

title: RasGas Begins LNG Exports, Doubling Capacity
reason: RasGas Train 1 started production and commenced LNG exports in August 1999, providing Qatar with a second major LNG production stream alongside Qatargas, with initial cargoes going to South Korea.

title: ICJ Awards Hawar Islands to Bahrain, Zubarah to Qatar
reason: The ICJ delivered its merits judgment on 16 March 2001 awarding the Hawar Islands to Bahrain and sovereignty over Zubarah and Janan Island to Qatar, resolving the decades-long bilateral dispute.

title: US Central Command Relocates to Al Udeid Air Base
reason: The US began moving CENTCOM's forward headquarters and the Combined Air Operations Center from Saudi Arabia's Prince Sultan Air Base to Al Udeid in Qatar in 2002–2003, with the full CAOC transfer completed in April 2003.

title: New Constitution Approved by Referendum
reason: Qatar held a constitutional referendum on 29 April 2003 in which over 98% of voters approved the permanent constitution, establishing limited legislative elections and enshrining civil liberties.

title: Chechen Separatist Leader Assassinated in Doha Car Bomb
reason: Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev was killed by a car bomb in Doha on 13 February 2004; two Russian GRU officers were convicted by a Qatari court and sentenced to life imprisonment, creating a serious diplomatic rift with Moscow.

title: Qatar Investment Authority Established
reason: The Qatar Investment Authority was founded in 2005 by Emir Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani via Amiri Decision to manage Qatar's hydrocarbon surpluses and diversify the national economy through global investments.

title: Al Jazeera English Channel Announced
reason: Al Jazeera officially announced plans to launch an English-language satellite service on 4 July 2005; the channel launched as Al Jazeera English on 15 November 2006.

title: Doha Centre for Media Freedom Founded
reason: The Doha Centre for Media Freedom was formally established by Emiri decree in December 2007 and opened in October 2008, not 2005 — a discrepancy of 2-3 years that places the founding event in the wrong year.

title: Qatar Brokers the Doha Agreement Ending Lebanon Crisis
reason: Qatar mediated talks among Lebanese factions in Doha, resulting in the Doha Agreement signed on 21 May 2008 that ended an 18-month political crisis by establishing a national unity government and appointing a new president.

title: Qatar Mandated to Mediate Darfur Peace Process
reason: In September 2008 the Arab League, at Syrian President Assad's suggestion, mandated Qatar to lead mediation between the Sudanese government and Darfur rebel factions, culminating years later in the Doha Document for Peace in Darfur.

title: Qatar National Vision 2030 Launched
reason: Qatar formally published Qatar National Vision 2030 in July 2008 and officially launched it in October 2008 via Amiri Decision No. 44, establishing a long-term framework for economic diversification and sustainable development.

title: Qatar Wins FIFA 2022 World Cup Hosting Rights
reason: FIFA's Executive Committee voted on 2 December 2010 in Zurich to award Qatar the 2022 World Cup, making it the first Middle Eastern country selected to host the tournament.

title: Qatar Reaches 77 Million Tonnes Annual LNG Capacity
reason: Qatar achieved its 77 million tonnes per year LNG production target in December 2010 when four new liquefaction trains came on stream, confirmed at a ceremony attended by Qatar's Energy Minister.

title: Qatar Joins NATO Intervention in Libya
reason: Qatar contributed six Mirage 2000-5 fighter jets and two C-17 transport aircraft to the NATO-led coalition in Libya, conducted air interdiction sorties, and supplied arms including French-made Milan missiles to rebel groups.

title: Doha Document for Peace in Darfur Signed
reason: The Doha Document for Peace in Darfur was signed on 14 July 2011 between the Sudanese government and the Liberation and Justice Movement after two-and-a-half years of Qatar-mediated negotiations.

title: Qatar Backs Syrian Opposition Against Assad Regime
reason: Qatar became one of the earliest Arab states backing the Syrian opposition from 2011 onwards, approving a $100 million fund for weapons acquisition and providing diplomatic, financial, and media support to rebel factions.

title: LNG Moratorium Imposed on North Field Development
reason: The North Field development moratorium was imposed in 2005, not 2012; all sources confirm a 12-year freeze from 2005 to 2017, making the stated year wrong by 7 years, well outside the ±5-year tolerance.

title: Emir Hamad Abdicates in Favor of Son Tamim
reason: Emir Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani voluntarily abdicated on 25 June 2013, transferring power to his son Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in a televised speech — the first uncontested succession in Qatar in a century.

title: Taliban Opens Political Office in Doha
reason: The Taliban's political office in Doha officially opened on 18 June 2013 at the request of the US government, providing the first formal diplomatic channel with the insurgency since 2001.

title: First Saudi-Led Diplomatic Crisis with Qatar
reason: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Bahrain withdrew their ambassadors from Doha on 5 March 2014 over Qatar's support for the Muslim Brotherhood and interference in internal affairs; Kuwaiti mediation restored ambassadors after eight months.

title: Qatar Joins Saudi-Led Coalition in Yemen War
reason: Qatar was among the founding members of the Saudi-led coalition that launched Operation Decisive Storm against Houthi rebels on 26 March 2015, contributing air force strikes; Qatar later withdrew from the coalition after the 2017 blockade.

title: Saudi-Led Quartet Imposes Land-Sea-Air Blockade
reason: On 5 June 2017 Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, and Egypt simultaneously severed diplomatic relations with Qatar, closed land/air/sea borders, and banned Qatari aircraft and ships — the most severe GCC crisis since the organization's founding.

title: Qatar Receives 13 Demands from Blockading Nations
reason: On 22 June 2017 the Saudi-led quartet delivered a list of 13 demands to Qatar via Kuwaiti mediation, including closing Al Jazeera, shutting the Turkish military base, and downgrading Iran ties; Qatar rejected all conditions.

title: Turkey Deploys Troops to Qatar During Blockade
reason: On 7 June 2017 the Turkish parliament fast-tracked troop deployment to Qatar; the first armed contingent of 23 military personnel arrived on 18 June 2017, supplementing an existing 88-strong Turkish force already stationed there.

title: North Field LNG Moratorium Lifted
reason: Qatar Petroleum announced the lifting of the 12-year North Field moratorium in April 2017, unveiling plans for a new gas project producing 2 billion cubic feet per day with an eventual 43% increase in LNG capacity.

title: Qatar Withdraws from OPEC
reason: Qatar's Energy Minister announced on 3 December 2018 that Qatar would formally exit OPEC on 1 January 2019 after nearly 60 years of membership, citing a strategic focus on natural gas; Qatar was the first Middle Eastern country to leave OPEC.

title: US-Taliban Peace Agreement Signed in Doha
reason: The US-Taliban Doha Accord was signed on 29 February 2020 in Doha by US envoy Khalilzad and Taliban deputy leader Mullah Baradar, outlining a 14-month US force withdrawal in exchange for Taliban counterterrorism commitments.

title: Qatar Abolishes Kafala Exit Visa and Reforms Labor Laws
reason: On 30 August 2020 Qatar announced sweeping labor reforms ending the requirement for employer permission to change jobs and introducing a non-discriminatory minimum wage of 1,000 QAR — the most comprehensive Gulf labor reform to date.

title: Al Ula Declaration Ends Three-and-a-Half-Year Blockade
reason: The Al-Ula Declaration was signed at the 41st GCC Summit on 5 January 2021, with Saudi Arabia and the blockading quartet restoring diplomatic relations with Qatar and reopening land, air, and sea routes.

title: Qatar Facilitates Mass Evacuation from Afghanistan
reason: Following the Taliban takeover of Kabul in August 2021, Al Udeid Air Base processed approximately 60,000 Afghan evacuees as part of Operation Allies Rescue which airlifted more than 124,000 people total.

title: Qatar Hosts FIFA World Cup
reason: Qatar hosted the FIFA World Cup from 20 November to 18 December 2022, the first edition in the Middle East and held during winter months; Qatar spent over $220 billion on infrastructure including new stadiums and a metro system.

title: Qatar Mediates Israel-Hamas Hostage Negotiations
reason: Qatar, alongside Egypt and the United States, brokered a temporary ceasefire and hostage-prisoner exchange agreement announced on 22 November 2023 that secured the release of 80 Israeli hostages in exchange for 240 Palestinian prisoners.

title: North Field Expansion Mega-Project Advances
reason: Construction on the North Field East and South expansion projects progressed in 2024, with QatarEnergy and partners Shell, TotalEnergies, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips targeting 126 million tonnes per year capacity by 2027.

title: Qatar Continues Gaza Ceasefire Shuttle Diplomacy
reason: Throughout 2024 Qatar sustained mediation alongside Egypt and the US; in May 2024 Hamas accepted a Qatari-Egyptian ceasefire proposal and in August 2024 the three mediators issued a joint 'bridging proposal' urging both sides to reach a deal.

title: Qatar Brokers Gaza Ceasefire Agreement
reason: Qatar's Prime Minister announced a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas on 15 January 2025, implemented from 19 January; the first phase involved the release of 33 Israeli hostages in exchange for approximately 1,900 Palestinian prisoners.
